newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian ad campaign for "Larry Flynt" terminated.
newsitem.headline: Belgian ad campaign for "Larry Flynt" terminated.

text.p: The controversial poster advertising campaign for Milos Forman's film "The People vs Larry Flynt" will end in Belgium from Tuesday, a spokeswoman for the distributor, Columbia Tristar Films said on Monday.
She insisted there was no connection between the end of the campaign for the film about the U.S. pornography king and a chorus of protests about the poster from religious groups.
"Tomorrow our campaign stops. It was only due to last for one week. It is a coincidence that some right-wingers have complained," the spokeswoman said.
The poster shows actor Woody Harrelson wearing a loin cloth and posing in the crucifix position, superimposed across a pair of bikini briefs being worn by a woman.
The poster, which has provoked protests in France and elsewhere, has already been withdrawn in the United States.

The film, which depicts the tumultuous life of publisher Larry Flynt, a school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful magazine Hustler in 1973, won the top "Golden Bear" prize on Monday for best film at the 47th Berlin film festival.
